late_fee: Varies by state, typically $15 or less
funding_speed: Often same day to 1 business day after approval
best_for: No credit history, small-dollar loans, building credit
perks: No minimum credit score: Oportun approves applicants with thin or no credit history using income and cash flow data instead
Small loan amounts from $300, useful when you need far less than the $1,000 to $5,000 minimums at mainstream lenders
Reports payments to credit bureaus, so on-time payments build a credit file
No prepayment penalty; paying off early cuts the total interest substantially
Fixed payments on a fixed schedule, unlike payday or tribal lenders this replaces
APR is capped at 36%, the widely cited ceiling for affordable small-dollar credit
drawbacks: APR range of roughly 19.9 to 36% as of mid-2026 is expensive compared with prime lenders; borrowers with good credit will beat it almost anywhere else
Origination fee of about 3 to 10% comes out of the loan proceeds, so a $1,000 loan may fund closer to $900
Maximum loan of $10,000 is low for debt consolidation
Not available in every state, and terms differ meaningfully by state
The 36% top rate on a 48-month term makes long terms costly; keep the term as short as the payment allows
